title: When a beneficiary’s rights become protected
shortTitle: When a beneficiary’s rights become protected
summary: Vesting concerns when contracting parties lose some freedom to modify or discharge a benefit promised to a third party without that beneficiary’s consent.
notes:
First establish that the person is an intended beneficiary with a right under the contract. Then examine the governing rule about events such as assent, reliance, or suit, and any reservation in the agreement. The assigned introductory materials distinguish the existence of a third-party benefit from the point at which the original parties can no longer freely alter it.

The syllabus assigns an introduction rather than every later case in the chapter. The complete Restatement text is in the Contracts Selections on file; a more detailed rule should be tied to the jurisdiction and assigned provision before use.

textbookImport.basis: Plain-language synthesis of the cited casebook passages; subject to the jurisdictional and source limits stated there.

topics.third-party-beneficiaries: Vesting affects the original parties’ power to alter an intended benefit.
